segments.text: A complete language model connects the components built in the preceding lessons.
Token IDs select token embeddings, which are combined with position embeddings.
The resulting sequence passes through stacked Transformer blocks and a final normalization.
A linear output head produces 65 logits for each position in the character vocabulary.
Count parameters in embeddings, attention, feed-forward layers, normalization and the output head. The reference untied model has 162,561 parameters.
Weight tying reuses the token embedding weights for the output projection. The shown tied configuration has 158,401 parameters; the difference is 4,160.
Before training, compare the loss with ln(65), approximately 4.174, the uniform-prediction baseline. Random logits need not give exactly uniform probabilities.
Try to overfit one small batch. A large drop in that batch’s loss indicates that the model and update path can learn those examples.
Poor loss on a fresh batch after memorizing one batch demonstrates why training fit alone is insufficient.
In an encoder–decoder model, cross-attention takes queries from the decoder and keys and values from the encoder output.
The decoder’s causal self-attention and its cross-attention serve different purposes: reading its own history and consulting the encoded input.
Pause: what determines the number of logits per position? What does the one-batch test establish?
The vocabulary determines the number of logits. One-batch fitting is a debugging check, not evidence of good performance on unseen data.
Recap the complete model and its sanity checks before training on the text corpus.
